In the morning, you will travel from Lima to the Pachacamac archaeological complex, approximately 30 km south of the city. Built of adobe, the complex overlooks the Pacific Ocean and the Lurín River valley. For more than 1,000 years, it served as an important religious centre and pilgrimage destination for the cultures that inhabited Peru.

After the arrival of the Incas, Pachacamac was adapted into an administrative centre, while local structures were preserved. During your visit, you will see the Temple of the Sun, Acllahuasi, Taurichumbi Palace, the Pilgrims' Plaza and other parts of the complex.

The Temple of the Sun and Temple of the Moon were used for ceremonies, sacrifices and prayers to the god Pachacamac. The route crosses a desert slope with views of the Pacific Ocean. In the complex's museum, you can see artefacts excavated on the site and learn about the religious history of ancient Peru.

The walking part begins in Independence Square, also called Plaza Grande, home to the Presidential Palace, Quito Cathedral and the municipal building.

Next, you will visit 2 important monuments of colonial architecture and the Quito School of art from the 17th–18th centuries: La Compañía de Jesús Church, with its gilded nave, and San Francisco Church with its monastery and religious art museum.

The route continues through Carmen Bajo, the Queen's Arch beside the City Museum, La Ronda street, Santo Domingo Church, Junín street and the San Marcos district. There will be a lunch break on Espejo street and time to explore the surrounding area independently.

In the afternoon, you will travel approximately 22 km north of Quito to the equator line. Here stand the Middle of the World monument and an ethnographic museum. You can take a photo with one foot in the Northern Hemisphere and the other in the Southern Hemisphere.

The Intiñan Museum is nearby. During the visit, a series of interactive experiments related to the equator's location is presented.

At the farm, you will learn how the balance, body, aroma and acidity of coffee are assessed.

A local expert will explain coffee's properties and demonstrate several common brewing methods, each bringing out the beans' flavour and aroma in a different way.

During the tasting, you will be offered a specially selected cup of coffee and coffee-based products that complement its flavour. Departure from the hotel is scheduled for 9:00.

Colonia del Sacramento is a former 17th-century Portuguese town recognised as a UNESCO World Heritage Site for its distinctive architecture. The trip begins with a short catamaran crossing of the Río de la Plata.

On arrival, lunch is planned, after which the route continues on a sightseeing bus. You will see well-kept parks, quiet streets and the waterfront, then reach the Real de San Carlos district with its historic bullring. After the guided tour, there will be free time to explore the town independently.

## Rio's Mountains and Tropical Forest

In Rio, a mountain can rise directly behind residential neighbourhoods, while forest greenery covers entire hillsides. A trip to Corcovado and Tijuca reveals just how close the city and nature are. Corcovado is home to the Christ the Redeemer statue, one of Brazil's most recognisable symbols. From the summit, the city looks different: dense buildings give way to the curves of the coastline and green mountains.

Tijuca forms part of a national park within Rio de Janeiro. The forest was restored after deforestation, and its history shows how people can bring a large natural area back into a city. Thick vegetation, humid air and the shade of trees are especially memorable after sunny streets and beaches.

This excursion suits visitors who want to combine Rio's famous landmark with its natural surroundings. Comfortable shoes and a light extra layer of clothing are a good idea. Visibility from the mountain depends on the weather, so the panorama is different each time.
